name: Darlux
summary: The AGS platform rebuilt Arabic-first for the Syrian market, with local payment methods and no dependency on Stripe.
oneLiner: Solar energy and batteries for Syria: Arabic by default, with local payment methods.

overview.what: A storefront and content management system for Darlux, a solar-energy and battery distributor in Damascus, built on the same platform as ags.ac.
overview.who: Customers in Syria who read Arabic first. English is available, but Arabic is the site's primary language.
overview.problem: Stripe doesn't operate in Syria, and making Arabic the primary language, rather than a translation, changes a great deal of layout.

roleDetail.summary: Full-stack developer: I adapted the platform for a new brand and market.
items: Forked the platform with a clean history and rebranded it: palette, logo, favicon and email templates
Made Arabic the default locale and moved English to /en
Made Stripe optional and added ShamCash and SyriatelCash as first-class payment methods
Ran a right-to-left audit that fixed 37 issues across 12 public components

architecture.caption: Locale and payment methods decided by configuration, not code.

components.title: Locale routing
components.body: Arabic is the unprefixed default; English lives at /en.

components.title: Country model
components.body: Syria's entry lists the payment methods checkout offers: ShamCash, SyriatelCash, cash on delivery and bank transfer.

components.title: Brand layer
components.body: One @theme block of design tokens re-skins the whole site, from buttons to transactional emails.

implementation.title: Internationalisation
implementation.body: next-intl with Arabic as the default locale and browser locale detection turned off, so the site is always Arabic first.

implementation.title: Payments
implementation.body: Checkout methods come from the Country model. The application builds and boots with no Stripe credentials at all.

implementation.title: Right-to-left details
implementation.body: Logical CSS properties throughout, phone numbers kept left-to-right inside Arabic text, carousel fades reversed, map legends and navbar categories translated.

implementation.title: Branding
implementation.body: Primary red #EE212E and the Darlux logo applied through the token layer, with brand colours carried into email templates and a footer logo inverted for dark backgrounds.

decisions.title: A clean repository for a sister brand
decisions.context: Darlux isn't AGS. Shared history would only be noise.
decisions.decision: Start from a clean git init and cherry-pick upstream fixes when they matter.
decisions.tradeoff: Fixes are copied deliberately. Four fixes landed in both repositories on the same day as the flagship: one bug fixed, three sites healed.

decisions.title: Arabic by configuration, not by redirect
decisions.context: The Saudi site uses an edge redirect so English URLs stay canonical. Darlux is essentially Arabic-only.
decisions.decision: Set Arabic as the default locale in configuration.
decisions.tradeoff: Simpler and total, and the right choice when Arabic is the site's main audience.

decisions.title: Make Stripe optional
decisions.context: No Stripe in the Syrian market.
decisions.decision: The app runs without any Stripe configuration; local payment methods are first-class.
decisions.tradeoff: One more conditional in checkout, and the same change later helped the Saudi and HMC sites, which don't use Stripe either.

challenges.problem: Making Arabic primary surfaced a long tail of layout bugs.
challenges.solution: One right-to-left audit: 37 fixes across 12 public components.

challenges.problem: Older content without a language tag disappeared once Arabic became the default.
challenges.solution: Items without a locale are still shown, so nothing silently vanished.

seo.title: Darlux · Arabic-first storefront for Syria
seo.description: Case study: the AGS platform adapted for Syria, Arabic by default, with ShamCash and SyriatelCash payments and a 37-fix right-to-left audit.
